label: Cicero, De oratore II.36: Historia as witness of times and light of truth

features.value: Historia vero testis temporum, lux veritatis

sources.citation: Cicero, De oratore II.36

notes: Classical rhetorical baseline. The later Clio inscription pluralises and redistributes the testimonial formula across Historia, Genealogia and Heraldica; direct textual dependence remains to be demonstrated.

label: Gisbert Cuper to Otto Sperling: coins as witnesses of time and truth
date_note: Letter dated at The Hague, III Cal. Nov.; year reconstructed from the surrounding dated correspondence in the 1737 printed edition.

features.value: coins as certissimi testes temporum and clarissima lux veritatis
history of kings arranged from coins

sources.citation: Gisbert Cuper to Otto Sperling, 30 Oct. 1691, printed in Giovanni Poleni (ed.), Utriusque Thesauri... Nova Supplementa, vol. 4 (Venice, 1737)

notes: Major prehistory of the Clio motto: Ciceronian testimonial language is explicitly transferred from Historia to coins. Verified in the early printed correspondence edition, not against the autograph letter.

label: Christian Schlegel, Historiae Saxonicae Antiquioris Veritas ex Nummis Demonstrata
date_note: Mulsow's article title dates the manuscript to 1697; a University of Erfurt research notice reports 1696. Preserve c.1696–1697 until the dating argument is fully collated.

features.value: historical truth demonstrated from coins
manuscript historical argument designed around coin evidence and copperplate tables
text and copperplate apparatus separated; plates later used in Weimar publication context

sources.citation: Martin Mulsow, Die erste Münzgeschichte des mittelalterlichen Sachsen..., Neues Archiv für sächsische Geschichte 89 (2018), 159–205
University of Erfurt, Wohl älteste Münzgeschichte Sachsens in Gotha entdeckt, 15 July 2019

notes: Do not infer a direct line to Köhler or the Clio plate. The significance is an earlier operational conjunction of historical truth, coins, genealogy and engraved reproduction.

label: Johann Georg Eccard to La Croze: comparative diplomatic method

features.value: collect specimens of scripts and seal impressions; compare them with coins and securely dated manuscripts; inspect archives

sources.citation: Johann Georg Eccard to Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze, Hanover, 10 July 1721, CAMENA transcription of Thesaurus Epistolicus Lacrozianus

notes: Direct evidence of an integrated comparison procedure across writing, seals, coins, dated manuscripts and archives immediately before the Weigel calendar launch.

label: Eccard: coins, seals and reproduced objects used to confirm genealogy
date_note: Public notice dated 23 Feb. 1722; letter to La Croze dated 29 Feb. 1722 in the printed source.

features.value: coins not merely ornament but strengthen/confirm genealogy
seals, coins and tombstones accurately drawn and engraved
when originals cannot travel, drawings and casts/impressions in isinglass, tin foil, wax, gypsum, lead or paper are accepted

sources.citation: Johann Georg Eccard, notice of 23 Feb. 1722 and letter to La Croze of 29 Feb. 1722, CAMENA transcription of Thesaurus Epistolicus Lacrozianus

notes: Strong operational prehistory: objects may circulate physically or through controlled surrogates, then enter genealogical argument through comparison and engraving.

label: Eccard, Historia genealogica principum Saxoniae superioris (1722)

features.value: demonstration from trustworthy and partly previously unknown monuments
catalogue descriptions report copperplates and genealogical tables

sources.citation: Google Books/Play digital record, Historia genealogica principum Saxoniae superioris, 1722

notes: Printed comparator for Eccard's correspondence-based working method. Plate contents require direct inspection before stronger claims.

label: Working hypothesis: Ciceronian testimonial authority redistributed to auxiliary/material witnesses
date_note: Target design enters the Weigel calendar between the 1724 negative witness and 1726 positive witness.

relations.note: Lexical/formula similarity: testis/testes temporum and veritas.
Earlier transfer of Ciceronian testimonial vocabulary from History to coin evidence.
Immediate prehistory of material and reproduced witnesses confirming genealogy.

notes: Do not describe as a proven textual genealogy. Current evidence supports rhetorical-operational convergence: testimonial authority once predicated of Historia is increasingly assigned to coins, seals, genealogy and heraldry as evidentiary instruments.

label: Johann David Köhler, Nutz der Wappenkenntnüß zur Entdeckung einer historischen Wahrheit

features.value: use of heraldic knowledge for the discovery of a historical truth
1518 Altötting silver votive ship reproduced on two copperplates; coats of arms and initials used to identify the associated Welf duke and companions

sources.citation: Johann David Köhler, Gezeigter und bestärckter Nutz der Wappenkenntnüß..., Göttingen, 1749
Altöttinger Bibliographie, Oettinger Heimatbund

notes: Important later articulation by the calendar editor: heraldry is explicitly cast as a procedure for resolving a disputed historical identification. Detailed procedural claims are supported by later scholarship and should be checked against the 1749 copy.

label: Köhler revisits Wilhelm Ernst Tentzel through a 1700 commemorative medal

features.value: Münz-Belustigung vol. 15, item 13 treats a 1700 medal of historian-numismatist Wilhelm Ernst Tentzel

sources.citation: Johann David Köhler, Historische Münz-Belustigung 15 (1743), 97–102

notes: This is a documentary bridge to the Schlegel/Tentzel antiquarian network, not proof that Köhler knew Schlegel's unpublished manuscript or borrowed its method.

label: 1751 printed response to Köhler's Altötting heraldic identification

features.value: printed Anzeige revisits the question of which Duke Heinrich owned the Altötting silver ship

sources.citation: Anzeige Zu der ... Frage..., Frankfurt/Leipzig, 1751; Georg Christian Gebauer attributed in catalogue records

notes: Shows that the heraldic identification became an object of printed checking and dispute rather than ending with Köhler's 1749 demonstration.

label: Araújo 2025: Evidentiary Authority as a System

sources.citation: André de Melo Araújo, Evidentiary Authority as a System: Johann Christoph Gatterer and the Collective Making of Historical Knowledge in the Eighteenth Century, Berichte zur Wissenschaftsgeschichte 48 (2025), 203–226

notes: Closest modern historiographical comparator. It reconstructs Gatterer's 1755 Historia genealogica as a verbal-visual-material information system and stresses collective/cumulative empiricism. Our corpus can test how far such practices extend backward into the 1690s–1720s and into serial calendar/numismatic formats.

label: Johann Christfried Sagittarius: numismatic surrogate-image project and later Schlegel correction
date_note: Project belongs to the 1680s; Sagittarius died in 1689. Preserve approximate dating until individual sheets are dated.

features.value: planned work on 600 bracteates in three books; 497 coin images cut in wood on four full sheets
images derived both from original coins and from received drawings
Schlegel inferred that the images were cut so Sagittarius could communicate to others what he possessed
Schlegel criticised the draughtsman for omitting names and sometimes transposing letters
Gotha copy bears Schlegel's handwritten identifications beneath the coin images

sources.citation: Martin Mulsow, Die erste Münzgeschichte des mittelalterlichen Sachsen..., Neues Archiv für sächsische Geschichte 89 (2018), esp. discussion of Johann Christfried Sagittarius

notes: Surviving annotated copy: FB Gotha, Ch. A 1205, Joan. Christfrid. Sagittarii ectypa numorum cavorum cum perbrevi explicatione Christiani Schlegelii manu adscripta. High-value prehistory for the double role of images as transportable scholarly surrogates and potential sources of evidentiary corruption.

label: Schlegel manuscript and copperplate apparatus as separable documentary lives
date_note: Manuscript c.1696–1697; later plate reuse reconstructed in 1723.

features.value: rough draft and fair-copy witnesses survive in Gotha
eight folio copperplate tables designed to represent more than 200 coins
manuscript and intended copperplates became separated; Mulsow reconstructs later publication/reuse of the plate apparatus in a 1723 Salomon Franck context

sources.citation: Martin Mulsow, Die erste Münzgeschichte des mittelalterlichen Sachsen..., Neues Archiv für sächsische Geschichte 89 (2018), 159–205

notes: Working shelfmark map from the scholarly reconstruction: FB Gotha Ch. B 1739 (rough draft) and Ch. B 1740 (fair copy). Verify shelfmark wording against manuscript catalogue before treating as primary object metadata. Material-history significance: plate history can diverge from the textual project for which plates were commissioned.

label: Documented Tentzel-to-Eccard textual use in Historia genealogica (1722)

relations.note: Do not read this target literally as a source chain; the shared authority is Wilhelm Ernst Tentzel. A dedicated Tentzel authority/source record remains to be created.

features.value: Eccard, Historia genealogica, col.331 prints Eneas verses after Tentzel's 1702 Supplementum Historiae Gothanae

sources.citation: Gottfried portal bibliography of Veldeke/Eneas print transmission, entry ECKHART 1722, col.331

notes: Bounded documentary edge: this demonstrates Eccard's use of material printed by Tentzel, not transfer of Tentzel's numismatic method. Köhler also engages Tentzel independently in 1743; the two edges should not be collapsed into a single influence chain.

label: Eccard, Erklärung eines alten Kleinodien-Kästleins aus dem Ebnerischen Cabinete (Nürnberg, 1725)

features.value: old jewel/casket from the Ebner cabinet in Nuremberg depicting the betrothal of Heinrich of Saxony/Count Palatine and Agnes
object used to elucidate Brunswick-Lüneburg history together with related old coins
current and historical copy descriptions report three copperplates; a current auction description adds one text copper, one woodcut initial, ornament and vignette
Peter Conrad Monath

sources.citation: Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek / Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, VD18 14444186
bavarikon / Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, 4 Bavar. 601, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb10332488-3
Joseph Baer & Co., Katalog 776 (1931), item 683

notes: Major local comparator: Eccard's object/coin/genealogical-historical practice appears in print in Nuremberg in the same year as the unresolved 1725 Weigel title copper. Different publisher (Monath); no direct Weigel/Köhler production link has been located. Treat as same-city operational context, not evidence of influence.

label: Leibniz: heraldic insignia tested by documentary testimony of antiquity

features.value: lion insignia attributed to Heinrich the Proud lack verae antiquitatis documentum; parallel Leibniz extracts use antiquitatis testimonium and antiquitatis documenta
related Schurzfleisch extracts are separately filed under Insignia and Genealogica
another extract from the same work is filed in the Sachsen-Lauenburg complex

sources.citation: Leibniz-Katalog, ID 4496, Ms 23, 47(1) Bl.48, Akademieausgabe V 1230.042; related IDs 66028, 66042, 26144, 4369 and 3540

notes: Direct operational prehistory for Heraldica as historical evidence: a heraldic antiquity claim is accepted or rejected according to documentary/testimonial evidence. Do not infer direct transmission to Weigel/Köhler.

label: Leibniz: insignia reconstructed through seals, dated diplomas and archive/tabularium carriers
date_note: Hoffmann Ehrenkleinod excerpts are catalogued after 1680; a Henninges Insignia excerpt is after June 1690. Exact individual dating remains to be tightened.

features.value: compare heraldic figures across seals and attach the seal evidence to dated diplomas and named archival/tabularium carriers
Leibniz explicitly doubts retrospective Welf armorial reconstructions and suspects projection from later French royal arms
successive Heinrich-der-Löwe and descendant seals are compared for blank shields, lion figures, banners and later heraldic changes

sources.citation: Leibniz-Katalog, IDs 42859, 68466, 68467 and 4222; Akademieausgabe V locators 1230.132, 4700.117/4-5, 1230.090

notes: Strong operational bridge between Heraldica and Diplomatics: arms are not treated only as blazons but as historically variable signs carried by dated seals/documents. Evidence is controlled through autograph-excerpt catalogue/critical-edition records; manuscript facsimiles remain to inspect.
